title: Gingival Bleeding and Von Willebrand Disease Typ 2 and 3
brief_summary: Von Willebrand disease (VWD) is the most common inherent bleeding disorder resulting in prolonged bleeding time. Gingival bleeding is a frequently reported symptom of VWD. However, gingival bleeding is also known as a leading symptom of plaque-induced gingivitis and untreated periodontal disease. Gingival bleeding in VWD patients may be triggered by gingival inflammation and not a genuine symptom. Thus, this study evaluates whether type 2 and 3 VWD determines an increased susceptibility to gingival bleeding in response to the oral biofilm.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria von Willebrand Patients:

* 18 - 80 years old
* no other bleeding disorder except 2 and 3 von Willebrand disease

Inclusion Criteria healthy controls:

* no bleeding disorder
* no anticoagulative medication

Exclusion Criteria von Willebrand Patients:

\- requirement of systemic antibiotics for measures that may cause transitory bacteraemia

Exclusion Criteria healthy controls:

\- bleeding disorder
study_population: Cases with type 2 and 3 VWD consecutively consulting the Haemophilia Centre, Medical Clinic III/Institute for Transfusion medicine, Hospital of the Johann Wolfgang Goethe-University Frankfurt/Main are asked to participate in this study as cases. For each case (VWD) a respective haematologically healthy matched control is recruited from the gingivitis and periodontitis patients of the Department of Periodontology, Centre for Dentistry and Oral Medicine (Carolinum), Johann Wolfgang Goethe-University Frankfurt/Main.
